note: valid/interleaved-tags is the corpus's only store whose `tags` arrays interleave owned and unowned entries — a plain tag between two @contexts (c1a2b3d1) and an @context between two plain tags (c1a2b3d2) — and its only records already carrying the `defer` marker (c1a2b3d3 with defer mid-array, c1a2b3d4 with defer alone). Every other multi-tag record in the corpus is contexts-first-then-tags, so merge_owned_slice could be implemented as 'owned prefix, then keep the rest' and pass the whole corpus; against this fixture that implementation produces the wrong bytes in five of the eleven recorded patches. It also supplies the two patch_deferred branches the corpus could not reach: the tags.delete clear branch (c1a2b3d3 deferred:false -> ["@home","research"]; c1a2b3d4 deferred:false -> the `tags` key removed entirely rather than emitted as []) and the equal-value no_change branch that must write zero bytes and consume no undo step. Outcomes were recorded by driving Store#edit_snapshot + Store#patch_task! — the protocol the slice ports — against a fresh copy per case under the pinned environment.

note: The corpus's three existing journal fixtures are all refusals, so nothing proved a successful replay against a Ruby-written journal and nothing shipped a cursor-behind-tip index. These two close both halves and were generated, not hand-assembled: the real CLI was run through five captures, a leaf delete, a refused parent delete, and a cascade delete under the pinned environment, and the resulting store plus journal were captured verbatim (only the org path templated). journal-undo-redo-delete ships that run at the tip — `tasks undo` replays the cascade delete and then the leaf delete, `tasks redo` replays both forward, and all four targets were verified with `cmp` against the files the generating run left on disk: byte-identical including `updated` stamps, so undo restores stamps rather than refreshing them. journal-redo-pending-delete is the same fixture after one more real `tasks undo`, giving eight states with cursor 6 — the only state in the corpus from which redo is reachable, and the one that drives the redo-tail truncation in Journal#record (a fresh capture there replaces state 7 and `tasks redo` then reports `nothing to redo`, exit 1). Both also carry the unlabelled `org_sha: null` baseline (the history predates the file) and the pluralized `delete 3 tasks: …` label the port must reproduce verbatim.
